title: Madfoon (Madfun)
tagline: “Buried” meat slow-cooked within the rice for an intensely infused, smoky dish.
intro: Madfoon means “buried” — a nod to its origins, where seasoned meat was wrapped and cooked buried in a pit of hot embers. In the Saudi kitchen it has become a close cousin of mandi: the spiced meat is nestled into the rice and slow-finished together, often with the dukhan smoke, so the grains drink up every drop of flavour. Rustic, smoky and satisfying.

items: 1.2 kg lamb or chicken, on the bone
500 g (2½ cups) basmati rice, soaked 30 min
Pinch of saffron in warm water
1 cinnamon stick, 4 cardamom, 4 cloves, 1 bay leaf

method: Brown the onions in oil, add ginger–garlic paste, then the spiced meat and sear well.
Add water to cover, season, and simmer until tender (about 1½ hours for lamb, 35 minutes for chicken). Reserve about 1 litre of broth; keep the meat.
Cook the drained rice in the measured broth with saffron and whole spices until nearly done, about 12 minutes.
Bury the meat down into the rice, cover and steam on the lowest heat a further 15 minutes.
Add the dukhan smoke (hot charcoal drizzled with ghee, pot sealed) for 5–10 minutes.
Uncover, lift the meat to the top, garnish and serve.
tips: Burying the meat in the rice is the point — it steams the grains with its juices.
A tight seal during the final steam keeps all the aroma in.
toServe: Serve with daqoos and a crisp salad.
